guide.title: Getting started
guide.description: All of GANIS in a few steps. Find it again anytime in Help › Getting started.

projects.title: Your projects
projects.text: The dashboard gathers your projects: novel, manga, film, series, game, tabletop RPG… Create one with “New project” (Ctrl+N); it opens right away.
points: Recently opened projects are at the top of the page.
Star a project to find it under “Favorites”.
Archive a finished project: it leaves the main list without being deleted.
The search bar filters projects by name or description.
A deleted project goes to the dashboard Trash: it can be restored there for 30 days, then it is permanently deleted.

spaces.title: Public space, private space
spaces.text: “Get started” opens the public space, without an account. Once signed in, you are in your private space. The two never mix.
points: Created without an account, a project is public: it is not encrypted, and anyone using GANIS on this computer can open, edit or delete it.
Created while signed in, a project is private: encrypted and only visible from your account.
To change it: project settings › Status and organization › Visibility.

Making a public project private requires signing in and typing its name again: it then disappears from the public space for everyone else. Making a private project public asks for confirmation: it is no longer encrypted.
Permanently deleting a public project (trash) requires typing its name again, because the other people on this computer lose it too.

layout.title: The workspace
layout.text: On the left, the module bar: Details, Characters, Locations, Structure, Plot, Notes and Search. The middle panel lists the module's features and items; each opens in a tab. Objects and Fauna and flora are added when you turn them on in the project settings.
points: Click a module again to collapse its panel.
Right-click a tab to pin it, or close the others, those on the left or on the right.
Pinned tabs come back the next time you open the project.
“Collapse” keeps only the icons in the left bar.

synopsis.title: The project home
synopsis.text: Every project starts with its sheet: synopsis, genres, tone and general information about the story.
points: Details › Project synopsis to write the summary.
Name, description and type are edited in the project settings.
The status (preparing, in progress, paused, done) helps track progress.

characters.title: Characters
characters.text: Create your characters: identity, looks and personality, with three levels of detail as needed.
points: Characters › Create a character, or Ctrl+N in the module.
The level of detail of the sheets is set in the project settings.
Add a portrait and an image gallery to each sheet.
Each sheet opens in its own tab, named after the character.
Colour palette: its colours frame the character's portrait.

locations.title: Locations
locations.text: From continent to room: each location has a sheet suited to its type (city, kingdom, forest…), and locations nest inside each other.
points: Locations › Create a location, then pick its type.
Place a location inside another to build your world's geography.
Add your own location types and statuses in the project settings.
Colour palette: as for characters, its colours frame the location's image.

world.title: Objects, fauna and flora
world.text: Two optional modules for the objects in your story (weapons, vehicles, phones, magic items…) and the animals and plants of your world. They stay hidden until you turn them on.
points: Project settings › Objects (or Fauna and flora): turn the module on, then keep only the categories you need.
An object can be stored in another (a key in a chest); a specific animal sits under its species.
A specific animal can also become a character: its character sheet is linked to it.
“Link an element” connects objects, species, characters and locations: “owns”, “lives in”, “part of”…

relations.title: Relationships and links
relations.text: Link your characters to each other (family, friendships, rivalries, alliances) and to their locations (home, origin…). The relationship graph shows your whole world at a glance.
points: Characters › Relationships to open the graph.
Character ↔ location links are managed from either sheet.
Structure items also show which characters and locations appear in them.

structure.title: Story structure
structure.text: Parts, chapters, scenes, or acts and sequences for a film: the outline adapts to the project type.
points: Structure › Story outline to build the tree.
Level names, numbering and colors are set in the project settings.
Each item has its own sheet, with its characters, locations and text.
“Move up” and “Move down” reorder the outline.

plot.title: The plot
plot.text: The plot board shows your storylines as columns, time flowing down, and their cause-and-effect links.
points: Add parallel storylines next to the main one.
Link two events: impact, influence or crossing.
Track each event's state: idea, draft, written, revised.
Plot › Read the story: the narrative in reading order.

notes.title: Notes and sticky notes
notes.text: Notes come with a real editor: headings, fonts, lists, tables, boxes, linked boxes and diagrams.
points: File your notes in folders.
The sticky-note wall holds loose ideas, placed freely.
Sheet descriptions also exist as system notes, editable from the notes.

search.title: Search
search.text: Find anything in the project: characters, locations, structure, documents, plot, notes and sticky notes.
points: The Search module looks through the whole project, ignoring accents and case.
Ctrl+K opens the palette: type to jump to an item or run a command.
Click a result to open it in a tab.

saving.title: Saving and versions
saving.text: A ● dot on a tab means unsaved changes. Save with Ctrl+S, or let autosave do it.
points: The status bar at the bottom always tells you where you stand: saving, saved or failed.
A version is created automatically at the start of each editing session.
“Versions” button: compare a previous state with the current one, then restore it if needed.
Name the current state to keep an important milestone.

trash.title: History, trash and undo
trash.text: A deletion can be undone right away with “Undo” (or Ctrl+Z). Deleted items stay 30 days in the trash.
points: Project › Trash to restore a deleted item.
Details › History: everything that happened in the project over the last 90 days.
In the history, click a name to open the item.

export.title: Back up and share
export.text: Export a project as a .ganix file to back it up or open it on another computer.
points: File › Export project (.ganix), or the download icon on the project card.
The .ganix file is not encrypted: keep it somewhere safe.
“Import a project” (with an account) adds it to your private space, or replaces an existing project after a backup.
Duplicate a project to try a variant without touching the original.

personalize.title: Your GANIS
personalize.text: Adapt the app to the way you work.
points: Light or dark theme in one click, in the top bar.
Packages: pick other color themes.
Settings: language, text size and account.
Work rhythm: your writing time day by day, and your streaks.

keyboard.title: Keyboard shortcuts
keyboard.text: Everything can be done from the keyboard too.
points: Ctrl+N create, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+W close the tab.
Ctrl+Tab switch tabs, Ctrl+K find anything.
Alt or F10 moves the keyboard to the menu bar.
Full list: Help › Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+/).

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.description: GANIS shortcuts. Editor shortcuts work inside a note.

actions.readStory: Read the whole story / exit reading

reference.undoDeletion: Undo the last deletion (outside a field)

about.tagline: The workshop for writers and screenwriters.
about.offline: GANIS works fully offline: your projects stay on this computer. Private projects are encrypted; public projects are not.
about.description: One place to build a story: characters, places, outline, plot, notes and documents, all linked, up to the readable version (▶ button).
about.dictionaries: Spelling dictionaries: French, Grammalecte (Olivier R., MPL 2.0); English, SCOWL (wordlist.sourceforge.net).

whatsNew.title: What's new
whatsNew.description: What changed in GANIS, version by version.

v0_1_0.title: Clarity and safety
items: A small window explains the public space (shared on this computer, not encrypted) when you click “Get started”; the “Public space” badge reopens it.
Making a public project private, or permanently deleting a public project, requires typing its name again.
The status bar no longer shows “Saved” after a hidden failure: “Last save failed” until the next successful save.
Key names follow the interface language (Shift / Maj, Esc / Échap…).
Messages use real singular and plural forms.
Edit › Paste works from the menu.
New: Help › Report a problem, to copy useful technical information.
Save messages (success or failure) appear as notifications at the bottom of the screen: the page no longer moves.
Double-click: on a row of the outline, progress or history, and in the reading table of contents, it opens the sheet; on a plot lane header, it renames the lane.

report.title: Report a problem
report.description: GANIS works offline: nothing is sent automatically. Describe the problem, copy the information, then paste it into your message.
report.whatLabel: What were you doing when the problem happened? (optional)
report.whatPlaceholder: E.g. I moved a scene on the plot board, then the error message appeared.
report.privacy: No project content and no account name: only the version, system, display settings and latest error messages. Read the text before sending it.
report.howToSend: Paste this text into your message (email, form, ticket) to the person or service who supports you with GANIS. A screenshot helps too.
report.copied: Information copied: paste it into your message.
report.copyFailed: Copying failed: select the text above and copy it with Ctrl+C.

center.title: GANIS Help
center.description: How each part of the app works, and answers to common questions.

workspace.title: The workspace
workspace.intro: A project opens in the workspace: modules on the left, panel in the middle, tabs in the centre.
items: The left bar gives access to the modules: Details, Characters, Locations, Structure, Notes, Search, and the project settings at the bottom.
The middle panel lists the module's features and items; a click opens a tab. Drag its right edge to widen it, or to the left to close it.
Tabs can be dragged. Right-click a tab to pin it, close the others, those to the right…
A ● dot on a tab means unsaved changes. The status bar at the bottom always shows whether everything is saved.
Ctrl+K opens the palette: type the name of a page, an action or an item to jump to it.

details.title: Project details
details.intro: The project home sums up your story; the synopsis tells it.
items: Project home: description, type, status and synopsis preview.
Synopsis: the story summary, with its genres, subgenres and tone.
History: everything created, edited, deleted or restored in the project, day by day.
Trash: items deleted less than 30 days ago, ready to restore.

characters.title: Characters
characters.intro: Each character has a sheet, images and relationships.
items: The sheet has three detail levels (essential, intermediate, advanced), chosen for the whole project in the settings.
Main image and reference gallery: drop images straight onto the sheet.
Relationships: family, friends, rivals… The relationship graph shows everyone at a glance; characters can be moved freely.
Locations: where the character lives, works, grew up — optionally with the part of the story concerned.
Colour palette: its colours frame the character's portrait.

locations.title: Locations
locations.intro: Locations nest: a continent contains kingdoms, which contain cities…
items: A location's type (city, forest, palace…) decides its sheet fields. You can create your own types in the settings.
The module panel shows locations as a tree; “Add a location in…” creates one inside another.
Each sheet has a banner, a gallery and the list of linked characters.
Colour palette: as for characters, its colours frame the location's image.

world.title: Objects, fauna and flora
world.intro: Optional modules, turned on in the project settings, built like locations.
items: Turn on Objects or Fauna and flora in Project settings: the module appears in the left bar. Turning it off deletes nothing.
Choose the categories you need (weapons, vehicles, magic…; fauna, flora): only those are offered when creating. You can also add your own types.
Fauna and flora: an entry is either a whole species, or a specific animal or plant, placed under its species.
A specific animal can also be a character: “Create its character sheet” or link it to an existing character. The character sheet shows it in return.
The “Links with objects and species” card connects these entries to characters, locations and each other, with a story period if needed (an object that changes hands).

structure.title: Story structure
structure.intro: Your story's outline, adapted to the project type.
items: Novel: parts, chapters, scenes. Film: acts, sequences, scenes. Manga: volumes, chapters, pages… Names can be changed in the project settings.
Numbers are computed for you; an item can be left out of the numbering (prologue, interlude).
Automatic numbering (renumbering on every move) is turned on in the project settings, as is each level's colour.
An item's sheet shows its summary, its characters (point of view, present…) and its locations.

Documents: in an item's sheet, keep its files (manga pages, PDFs, Word files, images, sounds…) with “Add files” or by drag and drop. They are stored in the project (encrypted if the project is private) and exported in the .ganix.

Click a document to read it in GANIS; “Read the pages” chains a chapter's images. “Edit in its application” opens it in Word, Acrobat, Clip Studio…: every save comes back, the previous content stays in the versions.

reading.title: Full reading (▶)
reading.intro: The ▶ button, on the right of the title bar, “runs” the project: the whole story is compiled in outline order and shown on its own, full screen.
items: Novel: the continuous manuscript, chapter after chapter.

Manga / comic: the story chapter by chapter, like a novel: what each chapter is about (its summary), then what its pages show, one after the other. Panel details (framing, balloons, sound effects…) stay in the page sheets.
Film, series, video game, role-playing game, custom project: each outline item with its summary, its text or documents, or failing that the plot events attached to it.
F5 does the same. Press again (or the ■ button) to return to the editing layout.
The reading updates itself: moving a scene in the outline moves it in the reading. It exports to Word, PDF or text.

plot.title: Plot
plot.intro: The board of parallel plots: one column per plot, time going down.
items: Double-click a column to place an event; drag cards to change their moment or plot.
Drag a card's round handle onto another to create a link: impact, influence or crossing.
Link each event to the project: point of view, characters present, location, structure chapter and notes.
“Story reading” shows the events in reading order (by default the structure's) with everything attached, chapter documents included.
Character, location and structure item sheets show their events under “In the plot”.
Ctrl+Z undoes each action on the board. The “Tension” button shows the tension curve; plot colours are set in Project settings › Plot.

notes.title: Notes and sticky notes
notes.intro: Everything that doesn't fit elsewhere: research, ideas, documentation.
items: The editor offers headings, fonts, sizes, colours, lists, tables and links. Less common tools are in the “…” menu at the end of the bar.
Sticky-note box: a coloured block in the text. Linked boxes: steps joined by arrows, with “+” to insert more. Diagram: boxes you move and connect with the mouse.
File notes in folders by dragging them in the panel; pin the most important ones.
The sticky-note wall holds loose ideas: move them by their strip, resize them by their corner.

search.title: Search
items: The Search module looks through characters, locations, structure, notes (including their content) and sticky notes.
Accents and capitals don't matter: “chateau” finds “Château”. Several words: all must appear.
Ctrl+K does the same from anywhere, and also offers pages and actions.

history.title: History, versions and trash
items: After a deletion, “Undo” appears for a few seconds (or Ctrl+Z outside a field). After that, the item stays 30 days in the trash.
Restoring an item also brings back everything that went with it: images, relationships, sub-items…

Versions: the “Versions” button of a note, the synopsis or a sheet shows its earlier states, compares them with the current one (removed in red, added in green) and lets you go back. The current state is kept before any restore.
A version is taken automatically at the start of each editing session; you can also create a named one (“Before rewrite”).
The project history (Details › History) lists every action of the last 90 days.

files.title: Projects, files and security
files.intro: Your projects stay on this computer.
items: Each private project is encrypted: without your password, its data can't be read. Public projects (created without an account) are not encrypted and can be opened by anyone who uses GANIS on this computer.
Export as .ganix (File › Export) makes a full copy of the project, to keep as a backup or open on another computer. Note: this file is not encrypted.
Import a .ganix (File › Import) adds the project, or replaces the existing one (a backup is made first).
GANIS works fully offline.

settings.title: Settings
items: Project settings (bottom of the left bar): information, statuses, character detail level, location types, structure and colours.
Objects, Fauna and flora: turn these optional modules on and choose their categories.
General settings (gear at the top): account, password, recovery key, language, theme, autosave.
Packages: colour themes for the whole app.

about.title: About GANIS
about.intro: GANIS is the workshop for authors and screenwriters: one place to build a story, from the first idea to a readable version.
items: For every kind of story: novel, manga / comic, film, series, video game, role-playing game, or a custom project with your own outline.
Characters, places, relations, outline, plot, notes and documents stay linked: what changes in one place shows everywhere.

Offline: GANIS relies on no online service. Your projects stay on this computer (private projects encrypted with your account, public projects unencrypted); a project travels elsewhere as a .ganix file.
Spell checking: Hunspell dictionaries for French (Grammalecte, MPL 2.0 licence) and English (SCOWL, wordlist.sourceforge.net).
Version, information and credits: Help menu › About GANIS.

items.a: Click “Undo” in the message that appears, or press Ctrl+Z. Later: Project › Trash, then “Restore”.

items.q: I edited a sheet and want to go back.
items.a: Open the sheet, click “Versions”, pick the state you want and click “Restore this version”.

items.q: How do I keep my manga chapter in GANIS?
items.a: Open the chapter's sheet (story outline › click the chapter), then “Add files” or drop all the pages on the “Documents” card. Put them in order (Alt+↑/↓), then “Read the pages” for continuous reading.

items.q: I edited a document in Word: is it up to date in GANIS?
items.a: Yes, if it was opened with “Edit in its application”: every save in Word comes back within seconds. Click “Finish” when you are done (the unencrypted working copy is then deleted).

items.q: How do I read my story in the order the reader discovers it?
items.a: Link the plot events to chapters (“Told in” field), then open Plot › Story reading: the order follows the structure. You can also choose a manual order at the top of the reading view.
Look at the status bar, bottom right: “Saved at …” means everything is saved. Ctrl+S saves the tab; “Save all” saves everything.
On the sign-in screen, choose “Forgot password” and enter your recovery key (6 groups of 6 characters), given when the account was created.

items.q: How do I work on another computer?
items.a: Export the project as .ganix (File › Export), copy the file, then import it in GANIS on the other computer.

items.q: Why don't chapter numbers change when I move them?
items.a: Automatic numbering is off by default. Turn it on in Project settings › Structure, or renumber by hand.

items.q: How do I rename “Part, Chapter, Scene”?
items.a: Project settings › Structure › Customise: each level's name, numbering and colour.
GANIS accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF, up to the size shown. Save the image again as JPEG or make it smaller.

items.q: I deleted a project by mistake.
items.a: Click “Undo” in the message that appears, or open Trash on the dashboard and choose “Restore”. A project stays in the trash for 30 days before being permanently deleted.

items.q: How do I lock GANIS when I step away?
items.a: Settings › Account › Automatic lock: choose a delay. After that time without activity, your password is required to resume; your tabs stay open.

items.q: I can't find objects or fauna and flora.
items.a: These modules are hidden by default. Open Project settings › Objects (or Fauna and flora) and turn them on: they appear in the left bar, under Locations.

items.q: My animal talks and has relationships: character or animal?
items.a: Both. Create it in Fauna and flora as “a specific animal or plant”, then click “Create its character sheet”. The two entries are linked.

items.q: How do I frame an entry's image with colours?
items.a: Add colours in the entry's “Colour palette” field (character, location, object, fauna and flora): a frame of those colours surrounds its image.
